title: Juliana Peralta, 13
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. (1) Montoya docket, ECF 36, joint status report filed 2026-07-31 (read in full from RECAP). The parties state they 'have executed a settlement agreement and at this time are awaiting necessary judicial approvals of a minor settlement'. They asked the court to set a 2026-10-29 deadline for a further joint status report if no notice of dismissal had been filed by then. This replaces the 'agreement in principle' status: the settlement is now executed but not yet court-approved, and the case has not been dismissed. No later RECAP filing (ECF 37 or later) could be retrieved, so whether a 2026-10-29 report or a dismissal was filed is unknown. (2) Character Technologies, Inc. filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition on 2026-10-12 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. The case is No. 26-11603 (BLS) before Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon, and the claims agent is Stretto (cases.stretto.com/chartech). Disney is the $20M stalking-horse bidder for an IP licence. The Debtor's bidding-procedures motion (Doc 15, filed 2026-10-13, read) attributes the filing partly to 'litigation and regulatory overhang'. The petition's list of the 20 largest unsecured creditors (Doc 1, read) includes three litigation claims marked contingent, unliquidated and disputed with amounts 'Unknown': the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the Commonwealth of Kentucky, and one '[Name Redacted] (Minor Plaintiff)'. The Peralta/Montoya plaintiffs are not identifiable in that list. No source I opened says whether the Montoya settlement was paid before the petition, or how the automatic stay affects it. Secondary reports (search snippets only, Futurism/Bloomberg Government, not verified) claim the January 2026 settlements had not been finalised or paid. CBS News (2026-10-13) confirms the filing but says nothing about settlement payment.
case_reference: Montoya v. Character Technologies, Inc., U.S. District Court, D. Colo. (Denver Division), No. 1:25-cv-02907-GPG-STV. Complaint filed 2025-09-15 before District Judge Gordon P. Gallagher and Magistrate Judge Scott T. Varholak. Key docket entries: ECF 31, joint motion to stay for settlement, 2026-01-06. ECF 33, order staying all proceedings pending mediation, 2026-01-07. ECF 34, joint status report reporting an agreement in principle, 2026-04-02. ECF 35, minute order setting a 2026-07-31 deadline for a status report or dismissal papers. ECF 36, joint status report, 2026-07-31: the settlement agreement has been executed and is 'awaiting necessary judicial approvals of a minor settlement'; the parties asked for a 2026-10-29 deadline for a further status report if no dismissal had been filed. A further minute order dated 2026-08-04 appears on the docket, but RECAP has no text for it. No dismissal entry was retrievable as of 2026-10-30. Related: defendant Character Technologies, Inc. filed for Chapter 11 on 2026-10-12, In re Character Technologies, Inc., U.S. Bankr. D. Del. No. 26-11603 (BLS), Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon. Its effect on this settlement is not public. No criminal case located.

title: Two Gangbuk District drug deaths
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. First-instance verdict, 2026-08-27, Seoul Northern District Court (source: Korea JoongAng Daily, 2026-08-27, and The Star/Korea Herald via ANN, 2026-08-27). Kim So-young was sentenced to life imprisonment plus 30 years of electronic location monitoring; prosecutors had sought death. She was acquitted of aggravated (special) injury for one of the six victims. The court rejected her claim that she meant only to sedate the men to fend off sexual assault, citing KakaoTalk messages. It found murder intent for the deaths and accepted that 'she does not appear to have recognized the specific risk of death' at first. On ChatGPT, the court said she came to understand the conditions under which the drugs could be fatal 'through ChatGPT and other sources' (JoongAng Daily wording); The Star/Korea Herald gives it as 'later used tools including ChatGPT to learn about the conditions under which the drugs could be fatal'. Appeals: Kim appealed on 2026-08-28. Prosecutors announced their appeal on 2026-09-02, arguing the sentence is too lenient and contesting the partial acquittal (JoongAng Daily, 2026-09-02). Appeal: Seoul High Court Criminal Division 7, presiding judge 구회근 (Koo Hoe-geun), first hearing 2026-10-21. The defence denied giving the pill-laced drinks to some victims and denied intent to kill. Prosecutors cited factual error, legal error and an unduly light sentence. The court set defendant questioning for 2026-12-09 and said it would close argument then (Yonhap via koreancenter.or.kr, 2026-10-21). The appeal report does not mention ChatGPT. Still no chat log published; the court's references describe ChatGPT as one information source on lethality, not as supplying a dose or encouragement.
official_findings: Seoul Northern District Court, first-instance judgment, 2026-08-27: guilty of murder, life imprisonment and 30 years' electronic monitoring; acquitted of one aggravated-injury count. The court found the defendant learned the conditions under which the benzodiazepines could be fatal 'through ChatGPT and other sources' (as reported by Korea JoongAng Daily and Korea Herald/ANN; the judgment text itself was not located). The judgment is under appeal by both sides.
case_reference: Republic of Korea v. Kim So-young. Investigated by Seoul Gangbuk Police Station; psychopathy assessment referred to prosecutors 2026-03-04. Indicted in custody by the Seoul Northern District Prosecutors' Office on 2026-03-10 for murder and special injury; additional indictment April 2026 for three further injury victims. Tried before Seoul Northern District Court, Criminal Division 14 (presiding judge Oh Byung-hee), charges of murder, special injury and violation of the Narcotics Control Act. Closing arguments 2026-08-18, prosecution demanded the death penalty. First-instance judgment 2026-08-27: life imprisonment plus 30 years' electronic location monitoring; acquitted of special injury as to one of six victims. Defendant appealed 2026-08-28; prosecution appealed (announced 2026-09-02). Appeal pending before Seoul High Court Criminal Division 7 (presiding judge Koo Hoe-geun / 구회근): first hearing 2026-10-21, defendant questioning and close of argument set for 2026-12-09. Korean case numbers not published in the sources located (searched 2026-10-30).

title: Joseph “Joe” Ceccanti
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. JCCP 5431 is no longer awaiting a judge. MLex (2026-08-04) reports that Judge Ethan P. Schulman of San Francisco Superior Court approved a plaintiffs' leadership structure for the coordinated ChatGPT product-liability cases: four co-lead counsel, one liaison counsel and a six-member steering committee. A secondary tracker (openclassactions.com, updated 2026-10-27; not a primary source) says this was Case Management Order No. 1. The same tracker says discovery was allowed to begin in late September 2026, that OpenAI's initial responses to the complaints were expected by 2026-10-30, and that no trial dates are set. These tracker points are unverified. No Fox-specific answer, demurrer or ruling was located, no chat exhibits have been released, and no settlement was found.
case_reference: Jennifer 'Kate' Fox, individually and as successor-in-interest to Decedent Joseph 'Joe' Martin Ceccanti v. OpenAI, Inc., OpenAI OpCo, LLC, OpenAI Holdings, LLC (and Samuel Altman). Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles, Case No. 25STCV32379, filed 2025-11-06. Coordinated into Judicial Council Coordination Proceeding No. 5431, 'ChatGPT Product Liability Cases', Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco; Order Re: Petition for Coordination granted 2026-02-03 by the Hon. Stephen M. Murphy after a 2026-01-30 hearing. Coordinated proceedings are now before Judge Ethan P. Schulman, who approved plaintiffs' leadership (four co-lead counsel, liaison counsel, six-member steering committee) on 2026-08-04 (MLex). Per an unverified secondary tracker, discovery opened in late September 2026 and OpenAI's initial responses were due 2026-10-30. Claims: strict product liability (design defect, failure to warn), negligence (design, failure to warn, negligence per se), UCL violation, wrongful death, survival. No criminal case located.

title: Two University of South Florida students
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. No development after 2026-08-24 found. Detail missing from the record: WUSF (2026-05-18) reports that the jury trial is scheduled to begin 2027-11-03. A secondary search summary says the judge called the date flexible and likely to change, and set a status hearing for 9am on 2026-12-10; I did not confirm these two points in an opened source. No public update was found on Florida Attorney General Uthmeier's criminal investigation of OpenAI after April 2026, and no charges against OpenAI.
case_reference: State of Florida v. Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh, Thirteenth Judicial Circuit, Hillsborough County, Florida. Arrested 2026-04-24; charges upgraded 2026-04-25 to two counts of first-degree premeditated murder with a weapon. A grand jury returned a seven-count indictment on 2026-05-06/2026-05-07: two counts of first-degree murder with a weapon (premeditated); tampering with physical evidence in a capital felony; two counts of unlawfully holding or moving a dead human body in unapproved conditions; and two counts of failure to report a death to the medical examiner or law enforcement with intent to conceal. The State filed a Notice of Intent to Seek the Death Penalty. Arraignment 2026-05-18; written not-guilty plea entered; jury trial scheduled to begin 2027-11-03 (WUSF). Specific circuit court case number not located (searched 2026-10-30). Separately, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI in April 2026 over the Florida State University shooting and expanded it on 2026-04-27 to include this case; no charging decision has been reported. No filed case against OpenAI located.
